about.title: Del Rey Oaks Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Del Rey Oaks is a small city, and many residents drive to nearby Monterey County facilities for hospital care, surgery, or specialist visits. When something goes wrong during that care — a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, a medication mix-up — it can be hard to know whether what happened was simply an unfortunate outcome or a departure from the standard of care a qualified provider owes a patient. California law treats these claims differently than a typical injury case, with shorter timelines, a required pre-suit notice, and rules about expert testimony. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take cases directly. Instead, we listen to what happened, then connect you at no cost with an independent attorney in our network who handles medical malpractice matters and can evaluate whether your situation may qualify for a claim.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Facts Matter in a California Malpractice Case

items.title: Strict, Short Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims to be filed within one year of discovering the injury, and no later than three years from the date it occurred. Waiting to sort out what happened can quietly cost you the ability to pursue a claim at all.

items.title: A Notice Period Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed, California law requires a 90-day notice to the provider. An attorney familiar with this step can help make sure it's handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A bad medical outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice — California cases nearly always require a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached. This is why an early, honest case evaluation matters.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery near Del Rey Oaks — does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law recognizes that medicine carries inherent risk, and a poor result alone doesn't establish that a provider was negligent. An attorney would need to review the medical records and, in most cases, get a qualified expert's opinion on whether the care fell below the accepted standard.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have one year from when you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no more than three years from when it happened. There's also a required 90-day notice to the provider before filing suit, so it's worth getting a case reviewed as soon as possible.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I could recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, and that cap adjusts upward each year under state law. Economic damages, like medical bills and lost income, are handled separately and aren't subject to that same cap.

items.question: Does LawProactive handle my malpractice case directly?
items.answer: No — we're a free connection service, not a law firm. We simply help you get in touch with an independent attorney in Monterey County who handles medical malpractice claims, and any representation happens on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
